{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABViNfpw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzg_DtRw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 57, "title": "Implement the minimal composable Node/Port pipeline runtime", "body": "## Problem

The product vision in #7 is now a local-first system composed of reusable processing nodes connected into pipelines.

The repository already has useful processing boundaries such as browser audio sources and `LocalAsrCore`, but they are still wired directly by product-specific application code.

Before adding processors such as translation or summarization, we need the smallest executable pipeline model that can compose real existing capabilities without introducing a speculative plugin framework.

The design should remain simple enough for the Web implementation, where local AI work commonly runs in Web Workers with WASM/WebGPU, while also allowing nodes whose implementation performs asynchronous external API or local I/O work.

## Expected outcome

Implement a minimal code-level pipeline runtime based on:

```text
Pipeline
├─ Node
│  ├─ input ports
│  └─ output ports
└─ Connection
   output port → input port
```

Validate it by expressing one existing transcription flow through the new runtime:

```text
Browser tab audio
        ↓ audio
Speech-to-Text
        ↓ final
Transcript output
```

The same runtime must allow the speech-to-text node to expose its existing provisional output without forcing provisional/final processing into separate nodes. There is no graphical node editor in this Issue.

## Design principles

### Node boundaries follow real processing boundaries

A Node represents an independently executable/configurable/replaceable processing unit. Do not split or combine nodes merely because data is realtime or final.

The current ASR may naturally remain one SpeechToTextNode with an audio input and provisional/final outputs. If a future design genuinely uses independent realtime and accurate models, those may instead be separate nodes. The runtime must support both shapes without domain-specific ASR rules.

### Data stays simple; relationships are explicit connections

Do not add generic provenance/source IDs or graph metadata to every payload. If downstream processing needs both an original value and a derived value, connect both explicitly through ports.

For example, a TranslationView can expose separate `original` and `translation` input ports fed by the original transcript and Translator output. The graph expresses dependencies; payloads should contain only the data required by their own contract.

### Multiple inputs and outputs

Nodes may have multiple typed input and output ports. One output may fan out to multiple downstream inputs, for example Transcript → Translator, Summarizer, and TranscriptView. Do not require one-input/one-output nodes.

### Async by default

Node lifecycle and input processing must support asynchronous implementations, including asynchronous start/load, receiving input, stop/drain, and dispose/cancel.

A node may emit zero, one, or many output values while processing. This must be sufficient for Web Worker + WASM/WebGPU processing, streaming model output, `fetch()` / external API processing, and IndexedDB or other local asynchronous I/O.

A slow asynchronous node must not globally block unrelated branches of the pipeline.

### Web execution model: one Node, one Worker by default

For Web nodes that perform substantial local processing, use the simple default:

```text
Node
  ↓
dedicated Web Worker
  ↓
WASM / WebGPU
  ↓
model
```

Do not introduce an implicit shared RuntimeManager, worker pool or model-sharing service. If a model/resource genuinely needs to be shared, represent that dependency explicitly as a Node/ports in a later concrete design.

Not every lightweight/source/view node is required to create a Worker; the rule is about ownership of substantial processing runtimes, not forcing DOM/UI wrappers into Workers.

### Explicit lifecycle and draining

Pipeline shutdown must preserve processing order. Stopping a streaming source must allow downstream nodes to flush/drain before disposal:

```text
source stops
  ↓
final source data
  ↓
processor flush/final output
  ↓
downstream drain
  ↓
pipeline stopped
```

Reuse the lessons from the existing ASR `stop → final → stopped` lifecycle. Cancel/dispose may discard pending work when explicitly requested.

## Scope

### Minimal runtime

Implement only the primitives needed by the existing transcription example:

- Pipeline;
- Node contract/base abstraction where useful;
- named input ports;
- named output ports;
- connections;
- output fan-out;
- asynchronous delivery;
- start;
- graceful stop/drain;
- immediate dispose/cancel;
- error propagation/isolation sufficient for the example;
- validation that only compatible declared port contracts can be connected.

Keep port typing small and practical. Do not build a general schema/type system.

### Existing capability adapters

Adapt existing components into the minimum real nodes needed to prove the design. At minimum, demonstrate:

- a browser-tab audio source node;
- a speech-to-text node that reuses the existing `LocalAsrCore`;
- a transcript/output node or equivalent sink suitable for deterministic testing.

The ASR node should expose the existing provisional and final outputs as separate ports/events. Do not rewrite ReazonSpeech/Silero internals or move ASR policy into the generic pipeline runtime.

### Product integration

Use the new pipeline for one existing browser-tab transcription path where practical, or provide an equivalently strong executable integration that proves the real source and ASR core compose through the runtime.

Do not migrate every existing UI/source in this Issue if that would expand scope without improving validation.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- A documented minimal Node/Port/Connection contract exists and matches #7.
- Pipeline code contains no ASR-, translation-, summarization- or model-specific routing logic.
- Nodes declare named input/output ports and incompatible/unknown connections fail clearly.
- One output can fan out to multiple downstream inputs.
- A node may have multiple input and output ports.
- Payloads used by the generic runtime are not required to carry generic source/provenance IDs; dependencies can be represented by explicit graph connections.
- Node input/lifecycle handling supports asynchronous implementations.
- A slow async branch does not prevent an independent branch from receiving the same upstream output.
- Nodes can emit multiple outputs over time.
- Graceful stop drains the demonstrated streaming pipeline before reporting completion.
- Immediate dispose/cancel prevents stale output from a previous run.
- The browser-tab → speech-to-text → transcript example runs through the new pipeline using the existing `LocalAsrCore`.
- Speech-to-text exposes both provisional and final outputs without duplicating the ASR model/pipeline.
- Existing ReazonSpeech ja-en/Silero/hayamimi behavior remains unchanged.
- Existing Web playground and Chrome extension behavior remain working unless an intentionally migrated path is explicitly documented.
- Deterministic tests cover connection validation, fan-out, async delivery, multiple outputs, lifecycle/draining, cancellation/stale output, and the real ASR adapter boundary.
- Current relevant unit/browser/extension tests pass.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Out of scope

Do not implement in this Issue:

- a graphical node editor;
- drag-and-drop graph editing;
- translation;
- summarization;
- topic extraction or visualization;
- a generic plugin marketplace/SDK;
- dynamic third-party code loading;
- a workflow DSL;
- persistence/serialization of arbitrary graphs;
- a shared RuntimeManager;
- worker pools;
- implicit model/resource sharing;
- distributed/server pipeline execution;
- a universal data/schema/provenance system;
- desktop/mobile native runtimes.

External-API-capable asynchronous nodes must be possible by contract, but no external API integration is required to prove this Issue.

## Context

Related:

- #7 — product vision: local-first composable processing pipeline
- #47 — reusable Local ASR Core
- #49 — browser-tab audio source
- #53 — current-tab Chrome extension
- #55 / #56 — documentation aligned with the new pipeline vision

This Issue intentionally proves the smallest runtime against existing working functionality before adding a second AI processor.
